title: Credit cards, pay-later and credit scores
blurb: Meena gets a credit card and a pay-later offer. See what they cost when you do not repay in full.
t1.title: The card and its free window
t1.b1: Meena gets her first credit card. She buys a bag with it and wonders when the money actually leaves her pocket.
t1.b2: A **credit card** lets you spend now and pay the bill later. If you pay the full bill by the due date, you usually pay no interest.
t1.b3: Think of a tea stall that lets you run a tab for a month. Settle it in full on the day and you pay nothing extra.
t1.b4.1: Example: Meena owes {exBal} on her card after the due date.
t1.b4.2: The card charges {rate} a year, so a month of interest is {exBal} x {rate} ÷ 12.
t1.b4.3: That is {exMonthInt} added to the bill for one month.
q1.prompt: Ravi leaves {bal} unpaid on his card at {rate} a year. How much interest is added in one month? Type a number in rupees.
q1.hint: Balance x yearly rate, then divide by 12.
q2.prompt: When do you usually pay no interest on a credit card?
q2.hint: Think of the tea stall tab.
q2.explain: Pay the full bill by the due date and the interest-free period means no interest.
q2.opt.a: When I pay any small part of the bill
q2.opt.b: When I pay the full bill by the due date
t2.title: Lab: the minimum payment trap
t2.b1.prompt: Open the lab. Try a small payment, then a bigger one. Watch how long the balance lasts and how much interest you pay.
t2.b2: Paying only the minimum due feels safe, because the card does not complain. But most of it goes to interest, so the balance shrinks very slowly.
q3.prompt: In the lab, set the balance to {bal}, the rate to {rate} and the payment to {pay}. How many months to clear it? Type a number.
q3.explain: Paying {pay} a month takes {months} months to clear {bal}.
q4.prompt: With the same settings, how much interest does Ravi pay in total? Type a number in rupees.
q4.hint: Read the red "Interest you pay" number.
q4.explain: He pays {totalInt} in interest on a {bal} balance.
q5.prompt: Meena says: "I pay the minimum every month, so I am fine." What is the best reply?
q5.hint: Look at the lab: how long did it take, and how much interest?
q5.explain: Paying only the minimum can take years and cost a lot of interest. Paying more clears it sooner.
q5.opt.a: Yes, the minimum clears the bill with no extra cost.
q5.fb.a: Paying the minimum is not fine. The unpaid balance keeps charging interest, so it takes much longer and costs more.
q5.opt.b: No, the rest keeps growing with interest, so pay more if you can.
q5.opt.c: Yes, as long as the card is not blocked.
t3.title: Pay-later offers and late fees
t3.b1: **Buy now, pay later** lets you take something home and pay in parts. It can look free, but the cost may hide in a higher price or in fees.
t3.b2: A "zero-cost EMI" still has a cost if you could have bought it cheaper with cash. Compare the plan total with the cash price.
t3.b3: "Zero-cost" only means no separate interest line. The shop may add the cost to the price or take away a cash discount.
q6.prompt: A phone costs {cash} in cash. The "zero-cost EMI" plan adds up to {planTotal}. How many rupees extra do you pay for the plan? Type a number.
q6.hint: Plan total minus the cash price.
q6.explain: {planTotal} minus {cash} is {noCostGap}. That is the hidden cost.
q7.prompt: A pay-later purchase of {buy} is missed, and a late fee of {fee} is charged. What percentage of the purchase is the fee? Type a percentage.
q7.hint: Fee ÷ purchase, written as a percentage.
q7.explain: {fee} ÷ {buy} is {feePct}. A late fee can cost more than a month of interest.
q8.prompt: Which statement about "zero-cost EMI" is best?
q8.explain: It may look free, but the cost can sit in the price. Compare it with the cash price.
q8.opt.a: It is always free, so I can ignore the numbers.
q8.fb.a: "Zero-cost" does not mean free. The cost can be moved into the price or a lost cash discount.
q8.opt.b: It is always more costly than a loan.
q8.opt.c: I should compare the plan total with the cash price.
t4.title: Your credit score
t4.b1: A **credit score** is a number that shows how reliably you have repaid money in the past. Lenders look at it to decide whether to lend to you.
t4.b2: Think of it as a trust meter. Repaying on time pushes it up. Late or missed payments pull it down. It builds slowly, so start early.
q9.prompt: Which habit helps build a good credit score?
q9.explain: Repaying on time shows lenders you can be trusted.
q9.opt.b: Paying late but paying in full
q10.prompt: What does a credit score tell a lender?
q10.hint: Look at the first card in this task.
q10.explain: It shows how reliably you have repaid in the past.
q10.opt.b: How reliably you have repaid before
t5.title: Education loan or scholarship?
t5.b1: A **scholarship** is money for your studies that you do not repay. An education loan must be repaid with interest, often after you finish.
t5.b2.1: Check scholarships first, since they cost nothing to repay.
t5.b2.2: For any loan, find the total repaid and the interest.
t5.b2.3: Compare the cost with what the course may help you earn.
q11.prompt: Asha takes an education loan of {eduP} at {eduR} a year for {eduM} months. How much interest does she pay in total? Type a number in rupees.
q11.hint: Find the monthly payment, multiply by the months, then subtract the amount borrowed. The loan lab from lesson 2 does this for you.
q11.explain: Over {eduM} months she pays {eduCost} in interest on top of {eduP}.
q12.prompt: What is the key difference between a scholarship and an education loan?
q12.hint: Which one must you pay back?
q12.explain: A scholarship is not repaid. A loan must be repaid with interest.
q12.opt.a: A scholarship must be repaid with interest.
q12.opt.c: A loan must be repaid; a scholarship does not.
glossary.borrow_credit_card.def: A card that lets you spend the lender's money now and repay later.
glossary.borrow_min_due.def: The smallest payment a card lets you make each month.
glossary.borrow_bnpl.def: Getting something now and paying for it in parts later.
glossary.borrow_credit_score.def: A number showing how reliably you have repaid past loans.
glossary.borrow_scholarship.def: Money for education that you do not have to repay.
